incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> reserved_capacity_threshold (tenant=aurorahealth, pool=aurora-prod-pool-3). Severity: page. Link: <https://pagerduty.local/PD123456>.

pagerduty: Alert PD123456 triggered, escalation level 1 -> oncall. Auto-assign: Alex (oncall).

Alex (oncall): Acked. I'm looking. p95 for /v1/generate for aurora-prod-pool-3 jumped from ~2300ms to ~7800ms and 503s at ~5% over last 2m. traffic steady at ~22 rps.

Maria (observability): Confirming metrics. KV cache evictions spiked at 09:12:03 UTC -> eviction rate 150/s. Disk IO wait on pool nodes rose; read latency from NVMe from 0.6ms -> 6.2ms. Sample logs: ```2026-03-15T09:12:05Z aurora-prod-pool-3-rt: kvcache: evict key=conversation:aurora:usr:xyz ttl=0 reason=mem_pressure
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z aurora-prod-pool-3-rt: http: 503 GET /v1/generate tenant=aurorahealth request_id=abc123 err=queue_full
```

Jake Infra: I see 2 pods restarted around 09:11 (OOM kill). Node m5-gpu-07 had high memory reclaim. Current replica count = 6. Recommend temporary scale to 9 to relieve KV pressure and give room for caches. Command I will run (internal tool):
```
internalctl reserved-capacity scale --tenant aurorahealth --pool aurora-prod-pool-3 --replicas 9 --reason "oncall scaling for eviction/503 spike"
```

Priya SRE: +1 to scale. Also enable soft-fallback routing to the fallback pool for non-SLA traffic while nodes start:
```
routingctl set-override --tenant aurorahealth --from-pool aurora-prod-pool-3 --to-pool aurora-fallback-shared --match "route!=/v1/interactive" --duration 15m
```
This will keep the interactive endpoints on the dedicated pool if possible. See runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-reserved#kv-eviction>.

Alex (oncall): Running the scale now. Running quick rate-limit to non-critical ep to protect pool: `rlctl set --tenant aurorahealth --limit 10rps --match route=/v1/batch`
Also creating incident bridge: https://zoom.bridge/incident/PD123456

Sam (CS): FYI pinged AuroraHealth ops contact (ops@aurorahealth). Told them we're investigating and doing mitigation. They asked for ETA; gave ~15min for scale to stabilize. Collecting any high-priority request IDs they saw.

Maria (observability): After scale action at 09:15:18 UTC replicas=9 started scheduling. Within ~90s eviction rate dropped to ~12/s. p95 dropped to ~1100ms and 503 rate down to 0.6%. Snapshot logs: ```2026-03-15T09:16:45Z aurora-prod-pool-3-rt: kvcache: eviction_rate=12/s
2026-03-15T09:16:47Z aurora-prod-pool-3-rt: http: 200 GET /v1/generate tenant=aurorahealth request_id=def456 latency=980ms
```

Alex (oncall): Verified traffic and metrics. Temporarily left replicas=9 for extra headroom. Removed non-critical rate-limit. Will keep routing override in place for 5 more minutes to ensure stability.

pagerduty: Alert PD123456 acknowledged by Alex (oncall) at 2026-03-15T09:13:02Z.

Priya SRE: Good containment. Please open an incident ticket for post-incident analysis: include timeline, root cause hypothesis (OOM -> KV eviction -> IO pressure), and follow-up actions: - Review memory usage patterns for aurora-prod-pool-3 models - Add autoscale threshold for eviction rate > 50/s to add nodes automatically - Harden VM swap / OOM killer settings - Update runbook with CLI snippets we used.

Sam (CS): AuroraHealth has requested a short incident summary to share with their engineering leadership. I'll draft and send once ticket has initial timeline.

Alex (oncall): Drafting P0 incident ticket now and will attach graphs. Marking as mitigation complete; leaving monitoring & follow-up to SRE team. Thanks all. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: PD123456 - resolved (mitigated) at 2026-03-15T09:18:19Z. Please file postmortem if required.

Priya SRE: Assigning postmortem to Maria (observability) and Jake Infra. CC: Alex for oncall notes, Sam for customer comms. Expecting postmortem draft in 48h.

Maria (observability): Will include dashboard panels and an instrumentation check to alert earlier on eviction trends.

Jake Infra: I'll look at node sizing and OOM tuning; propose a follow-up RFC if we need instance-type change.

Alex (oncall): Closing this thread from oncall perspective. Reopen if we see regression.
